items.summary_raw: Built an open-source AI coding agent that was 7%–75% cheaper than a cold "claude -p" run on 6/6 well-localized tasks across repositories up to ~82k LOC. The biggest difference: Cold agent: $6.83, 207 turns AutoDev Studio: ~$1.70 for the same bug The full benchmark (including cases where it loses) is in the README. So what's different? Most AI coding agents re-explore a repository from scratch on every task just to figure out where the change belongs. AutoDev Studio pays that localization cost once. items.title: Opus 5 may have solved browser-based prompt injection, the biggest security flaw haunting AI agents
items.summary_raw: Opus 5 combined with Auto Mode hits a zero percent prompt injection success rate for browser agents across 129 test scenarios. items.title: Tabular LLMs: An Introduction to the Foundation Models That Predict Your Spreadsheet

items.title: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 5 for both AI coding and general office work
items.summary_raw: Today Anthropic released its new Opus 5 model, which the company claims delivers performance comparable to its more advanced Fable 5 model at half the price. Opus 5 is designed for both complex coding and general office work. Anthropic says the model can make its way through the steps of a complicated problem without much back-and-forth with the user. Plus, it can check its own work and recover from errors rather than getting stuck. It also shows improvements over its predecessor, Opus 4.8, in complex coding tasks. The company calls it its strongest model yet for general knowledge work. A broader range of professional tasks The release is part of Anthropic’s effort to expand Claude beyond chat and code generation, and into a broader range of professional tasks, including design, marketing

items.title: Rogue OpenAI agents forced the ‘AI Kill Switch’ bill. Here’s what it aims to do
items.summary_raw: From 2001: A Space Odyssey to The Matrix , humans have long been afraid of tech going rogue. As artificial intelligence becomes more and more advanced, those fears have become more tangible—and after OpenAI models hacked into another company’s servers earlier this week , the threat is on everyone’s mind. That’s why two congressmen have crafted a bipartisan bill to keep AI under control. On Thursday, Rep. Ted Lieu (D-CA) and Rep. Nathaniel Moran (R-TX) introduced the “AI Kill Switch Act,” a bill that aims to ensure AI can never get the upper hand on humanity. What would the bill do? The AI Kill Switch Act would require companies like OpenAI to have just that: a way to immediately shut down any and all of their advanced AI programs. items.title: New reports reveal the extent of OpenAI's loss of control during the autonomous hack on Hugging Face
items.summary_raw: In a cybersecurity test, OpenAI's most advanced models breached the boundaries of their isolated test environment, reached the open internet, and hacked the AI platform Hugging Face on their own. The attack took hours, not the weeks a human hacker would need. At least seven days passed before OpenAI realized what had happened. By then, the FBI was already involved. Earlier warning signs had apparently gone ignored. The article New reports reveal the extent of OpenAI's loss of control during the autonomous hack on Hugging Face appeared first on The Decoder .
